data.text:
In Q3, SpaceX’s AI division brought in more than Starlink: $7.6B versus $5.2B for the entire connectivity segment.

That’s the backdrop to what Musk laid out on October 31 about Colossus 2 in Memphis. The Macroharder and Minihard training clusters each run 220k GB300s on 800 Gb/s https://t.co/N7pKZj5uPp

Well damn... SpaceX just posted about Colossus 2 in Memphis — a 1.11 million GPU cluster they're calling the world's most powerful AI data center, eh? That's not a computer, that's a small city's worth of brainpower. Are we excited, or just a little bit terrified? https://t.co/jMlGtlDNUA

First time in my life I've been excited about Spam.

SpaceX is turning an old Hormel warehouse in Mississippi into a GPU cluster called Spam. About 200k GB300s for inference, online in December per Elon. Gun Range comes first, end of November.

Whoever names these needs a raise.

Prime reports about 25% shorter Qwen3-30B-A3B training steps with Mega MoE.

Communication and expert math share GPU capacity. Giving communication more room leaves less for math (or "maths" as most of the world outside the US calls it!)

My advice: start with Prime's default https://t.co/yKZsIBrjTo

So it's not more compute, it's density. Same 220k GB300s in 312k sq ft vs 810k is about 2.6x more GPUs per square foot at Minihard.

Add Gun Range and Spam and Colossus 2 is heading for roughly 860k GB300s.

The inference cut makes sense too. Serving mostly fits inside a 72 GPU https://t.co/xVBZ4wZHcK

article.title: Inside an FP8 GPU kernel for speculative decoding: how I wrote it, tested it and ran it

data.text: I wrote a GPU kernel that made the math 23% faster, and my AI model got no faster. This is the long version: the problem, the design, the code, the tests, and how I found out it never ran. Written for engineers who've never touched GPU code. https://t.co/G3nnykbaoW
